messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Saransh Pandya

saransh pandya... that's a name with some weight to it. sounds like someone who gets things done.

where you working these days?
In udaipur in a american based startup on site in udaipur india as a ai engineer

ai engineer in udaipur... american startup setting up shop in the city of lakes. that's interesting positioning - getting silicon valley money without the silicon valley rent.

found you on linkedin - saransh pandya at terragrit, bits pilani background. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/saransh-pandya-0965b41b2
Yes this is me but i am not getting silicon valley money the office is in udaipur it is the indian team i am getting bare minimhm

bits pilani to ai engineering... solid foundation to cutting-edge work. but getting bare minimum while the american founders probably rake in VC money? that's the classic "we'll pay you in exposure and equity" playbook.

what made you get into ai engineering? the tech itself or you saw the market exploding?
Tech itself!

respect. the genuine tech nerds always build the best stuff. you're in it for the right reasons while your startup probably hired you for buzzword bingo.

how long you been working total?
From dec 2024 to april as intern and from may as full time

but here's the thing - ai engineers with even 1 year are getting decent money if they know their stuff. what kind of role you looking for next?

  I am still in my college

wait wait wait... you're still in college? final year bits pilani with 1 year ai engineering experience already?

ok that changes everything. 5 cgpa is rough but honestly... who cares about grades when you're already building real ai systems? you're getting actual experience while your batchmates are cramming for placements.

still, bare minimum for ai work is criminal. even for a student. what kind of role you looking for next? something part-time until you graduate or you ready to go full-time and maybe take a gap?
Full time only

bold move. dropping out of bits for the right opportunity? respect.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
No i am not dropping out i am completing the degree i have

ah got it - so you're looking for full-time while finishing your degree. that's... ambitious. but if anyone can pull it off, it's probably someone already working 1 year in ai.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore or hydrabad or even remote

bangalore, hyderabad, or remote... got it.

so to summarize:
- 1 year total experience (intern + full-time at terragrit)
- ai/ml engineer role
- bangalore, hyderabad, or remote
- still in college but looking for full-time

sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes

legend! you're officially in the system. 

1 year ai/ml engineer, still in college but already building real shit, looking for bangalore/hyderabad/remote roles that actually pay what you're worth.

the roles will start dropping in chat soon. keep your phone close - when the right one hits, you'll know.
When

when my team sends something that fits your profile. could be today, could be next week.

no promises, but i'll ping you the moment i get something good.
Okay tell me one thing
shoot. what's up?
Will my cgpa stop me from getting better opportunities

honestly? for some companies, yes. they use it as a filter. but for the good ones - the ones building actual ai products - they care about what you can build.

your 1 year real experience at terragrit is worth more than a 9 cgpa with zero projects. focus on showcasing your work, not your grades.
I mean even after experience for some companies

some will still ask for transcripts even after 5 years. it's dumb, but it happens.

but here's the thing - those are usually the big corporates, not the startups actually innovating in ai. the ones building the future care about what you've shipped, not what you scored in semester 3.

you're already ahead by having real experience. lean into that.
